content: A piped link is a hyperlink within a project or to a related sister project that displays a label different from the actual name of the page it links to. This feature allows users to embed links within the text of a page in a seamless manner, avoiding the need for phrases like see also, even when the wording of the link does not exactly match the title of the target page. Depending on the browser and user preferences, the actual destination of the link can still be identified. When hovering over the link, the target page's name appears in a tooltip or the status bar. For example, a link labeled How to set up a coffee house might redirect to a page with a different title. The term piped refers to the use of the pipe character | to separate the displayed label from the actual link. This character is named after its alternative use in computing, as seen in the concept of a pipe in programming. For instance, a piped link might display the word station in an article about trains, where the context makes it clear that the link refers to a train station. This approach is more user-friendly than linking to a disambiguation page titled station. Using Redirects as an Alternative An alternative to piped links is the use of redirect pages. For example, a link labeled How to set up a coffee house could directly point to a redirect page with the same title. However, this method has certain limitations: 1. The tooltip that appears when hovering over the link does not reveal the actual target page. 2. The Related changes feature in the project will show changes to the redirect page rather than the target page. 3. The redirect message on the target page may slightly clutter its appearance. In some cases, it may be preferable for the link's label to provide additional information not included in the target page's title. For instance, a link might display a unit's value in terms of other units. In such cases, a redirect page can be created with the desired label, which then points to the appropriately named target page. For example, a page titled 30.48 cm could redirect to a page about the Foot (unit of length). Automatic Conversion of Wikitext: The Pipe Trick The pipe trick is a feature that simplifies the creation of piped links. If the portion of the link after the | character is left empty, the system automatically converts it into an abbreviated form of the target page's name. The conversion follows these rules: 1. Any namespace prefix (e.g., Help:) or interwiki prefix (e.g., commons:) is removed. 2. Text in parentheses at the end of the page name is removed. 3. If there are no parentheses but a comma is present, the comma and everything following it are removed. For example: A link to en:Pipe with an empty pipe trick will render as Pipe. A link to Template:Example will render as Template. A link to Boston, Massachusetts will render as Boston. When previewing a page, the result of the pipe trick is visible in the preview, but the conversion is not yet reflected in the edit box. After saving and reopening the edit box, the conversion becomes visible. However, the pipe trick has limitations in certain contexts, such as links between different language versions of Wikipedia or Wiktionary, where it may not function as intended. Inverse Pipe Trick The inverse pipe trick works in the opposite direction. For example, on a page titled A (c), a link to A will automatically be converted to A (c). Similarly, on a page titled A, c, a link to A will be converted to A, c. Syntax for External Links For external links, a space is used instead of the pipe character to separate the displayed label from the URL. This is part of a broader concept referred to as clean links. For more details, refer to the relevant editing guidelines.
